newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union ends jobs summit with call to action.
newsitem.headline: German union ends jobs summit with call to action.

text.p: Germany's top trade union official on Wednesday closed a high-profile conference on job creation with a call for unions, politicians and employers to act immediately to solve the country's jobless crisis.

But German Trade Union Federation chief Dieter Schulte admitted that wide divisions on the issue remained among the 500-plus participants at the conference, which included representatives from those three groupings.
"But people desperately want us to stop talking and start doing something concrete," Schulte told the conference.
"We are not talking about abstract numbers but about 4.5 million people and their families," he said, referring to March unemployment data published on Tuesday.

Schulte acknowledged that no great breakthrough had been achieved at the conference, but a dialogue was now in place that had not existed since the failure of last year's so-called "Alliance for Jobs" pact between unions, government and employers.
"Every small step is an important one," Schulte urged, insisting there were no quick fixes to Germany's high unemployment levels.

Schulte pointed to signs of agreement on the need for a reduction of Germany's high non-wage labour costs and for efforts to tackle its illegal labour market as indications that the conference had made some achievements.
He added that there had been consensus among the participants that investment in job-creating areas such as research and development should also be supported.
